A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LUDVIG. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v4 reports original segmentation, localization, ablation and runtime results on NVOS, SPIn-NeRF and LERF, including per-scene appendix results.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and additionally reports ScanNet semantic segmentation, LERF 3D object selection and new qualitative demonstrations.

M1.justification: The core aggregation and graph-diffusion algorithms remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds a downstream adaptation using automatically generated SAM regions with object-level CLIP features, followed by assigning each Gaussian its highest-similarity text label, replacing OpenGaussian's feature-learning stage.

E1.justification: v5 adds ScanNetv2 evaluation with point-level, multiclass semantic labeling of indoor scenes, substantially extending the earlier object-selection and localization coverage. It also adds a CO3D teddy-bear removal demonstration. NVOS, SPIn-NeRF and LERF coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v5 Table 4 adds comparisons against OpenGaussian and Dr. Splat under the 3D-selection protocol. Table 6 evaluates against LangSplat, LEGaussians and OpenGaussian on ScanNet. OpenGaussian and LEGaussians were previously discussed or cited but lacked these reported comparisons; existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v5 adds a LERF protocol that binarizes 3D features before rendering, separately from the retained 2D-segmentation protocol. ScanNet evaluation initializes Gaussians from ground-truth points, fixes their positions, disables densification, and reports mIoU and mAcc for 19-, 15- and 10-class settings. These are added protocols, not demonstrated revisions to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v5 adds text-prompt object-removal case studies in Figures 1 and 5, a ScanNet feature-coherence visualization in Figure F, and comparative training/inference runtime analysis in Appendix B.2. The existing SPIn-NeRF and LERF component ablations and earlier qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three independent runs. The statistical reporting practice remains unchanged, without added seed lists, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing segmentation scores, ablations and per-scene runtime entries match. New ScanNet results include 19-class mIoU of 33.9 for LUDVIG versus 24.7 for OpenGaussian. New LERF 3D-selection results report overall IoU of 50.4 versus 43.1 and 43.6 for OpenGaussian and Dr. Splat; these use different conditions from the retained 64.3 2D-segmentation result. The main-text uplifting time changes from 1.3 to about 2 ms per view and feature dimension, matching the earlier appendix.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the aggregation/gradient-step connection, graph construction and diffusion mathematics are retained. There are no added or substantively revised formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces its third contribution about combining SAM and diffusion with a claim that uplifting can replace other methods' feature learning and yield accuracy gains. The conclusion correspondingly presents LUDVIG as a reusable module across applications. This materially expands the contribution framing while retaining the original aggregation and diffusion claims.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly qualifies runtime comparisons because hardware may differ, discusses using SAM-based preprocessing when inference latency matters, and interprets coherent ScanNet features despite constrained reconstruction. Section 6 removes the earlier explicit limitation concerning high-frequency regions while retaining reconstruction-quality, specularity and blur limitations.

D1.justification: v5 documents the ScanNet reconstruction and feature-generation setup and adds comparative stage and per-query timings. It revises the reported GPU designation from A6000 ADA to RTX 6000 ADA, without establishing a hardware replacement. Existing Appendix A hyperparameters and the project-page access information remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds Dr. Splat, manifold denoising, ScanNet, CO3D and Panst3R citations, clarifies OpenGaussian's learned pseudo-features, and cites Panst3R as an application of uplifting. AbsGS and FreGS references disappear with the high-frequency limitation. The overall related-work framework remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the introduction and downstream-task explanations are rewritten and condensed. Experiments are reorganized around task/setup/results descriptions, runtime analysis becomes a separate appendix section, and a contents page is added. These changes extend beyond wording associated with the new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. The combined LERF table is split and expanded; ScanNet and comparative-runtime tables are added, alongside overview, object-removal and ScanNet-feature figures. Earlier qualitative panels are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central uplifting claim. Unlike v4's main comparisons between complete pipelines, the ScanNet experiment holds feature maps and reconstruction settings fixed while replacing OpenGaussian's feature-learning stage. The separate LERF 3D-selection evaluation also tests features without relying on post-rendering SAM segmentation. Appendix B better exposes preprocessing/inference tradeoffs. Inconsistent ScanNet mask-generation wording between Sections 4.3 and 5.4 remains a limited weakness, but the stronger controls and direct 3D evaluation provide a substantial net quality improvement.
